name: avatar

frames.best_why: Both rows are fully lit with every face and fallback visible and no cursor near them.

tagline: Round face photos that drop back to grey initials when missing.
summary: User portraits shown as clipped circles, with a grey initials fallback when a picture is unavailable, plus an overlapping stack of smaller faces that ends in a plus-eight counter.
appearance: Two rows on black. The top row has six large round portraits: four photos, a grey circle reading JL and a softened-square portrait. Below, five small round photos overlap and end in a grey circle reading +8.
behaviour: Static: nothing moves. Photos simply fill their circles, and a missing or failed image would swap to initials on a flat grey circle.
demo_content: Portrait photos of named people, a grey JL fallback, a square-cornered portrait and a stacked group ending in +8.
search_phrases: round profile picture for a user
image that falls back to letters
stacked profile icons with a count
use_when: You show people by face and need a tidy fallback when a photo is missing or fails.
avoid_when: Falls back to dull initials, and the demo pulls images from an external placeholder service.
customise: You supply the image and the fallback as children; size and corner radius come from className, and the fallback text is whatever you put inside it.
weight_why: Remote images clipped to a circle; no animation or script beyond image loading.

a11y.note: Images carry alt text in the demo and fallbacks show initials; the decorative stack images are given an empty alt.

issues: The square portrait and grey JL circle sit in a row of round faces, which reads as accidental
Every frame is the same, so loading and fallback states are never actually shown
polish_why: Neat photo set with a working initials fallback; the mixed round and square shapes clash.
title: Avatar
